subject: Post-demo alignment: eval prompt batch + model recommendations
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Li <emma@lighthouse.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 21 Jun 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: next steps for eval prompts and sample set

Hi Emma — thanks again for taking the demo earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

- Goal: produce a 200–300 prompt sample batch that represents Lighthouse's most frequent and edge-case queries for a 2-week eval.
- Deliverables we requested during the call: customer query samples (anonymized), 10–15 high-risk edge cases (legal/regulatory sensitive), and your redaction constraints for PHI/PPI.
- Redwood recommendations: start with two model families for the eval (an instruction-tuned open LLM and a quantized 8-bit variant for cost baseline). I’ll include concrete models and benchmark links in the follow-up.

Can you confirm the timeline below?
1) Share initial 100 sample prompts + redaction rubric by Tue 6/26
2) We'll supplement to 200 with synthetic edgecase expansion by Fri 6/29
3) Redwood runs benchmarks + baseline eval dashboard by 7/6

Attachments: lh_prompt_template.csv (empty CSV template) — I attached a quick template to make collection easier.

If procurement wants a copy of the model benchmark plan we can include that in the HubSpot record. Next step: Emma, can you share who will own the prompt extraction on your side?

Thanks,
Rafael
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: lh_prompt_template.csv (csv))

From: Emma Li <emma@lighthouse.health>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lighthouse Health Procurement <procurement@lighthouse.health>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 21 Jun 2028 18:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: next steps for eval prompts and sample set

Rafael — appreciate the concise recap. Confirming team ownership and a couple clarifications: 

- I'll own the prompt extraction but will pull in our Data Privacy lead for redaction rubrics (cc'd procurement for scheduling).
- We can share 120 real queries by 6/26; the remaining items may include logged support chats which require a second review.
- Edge cases: our legal team flagged two categories we consider "high sensitivity": "patient-identifying sequences" and "insurance claim denials with provider details". We'll supply examples but ask Redwood to advise on redaction best practices for both.

Quick Qs:
1) Which exact model families are you recommending for the two-track eval (cost vs accuracy)?
2) How granular are the benchmark metrics — e.g., token-level latency, hallucination rate on a labeled set, and privacy leakage indicators?

We look forward to the prompt template and sample from your side.

—Emma
Director of Product, Lighthouse Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, Emma Li <emma@lighthouse.health>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 22 Jun 2028 09:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: next steps for eval prompts and sample set

Emma / Rafael — adding model and eval specifics so you have something actionable. Rafael, feel free to paste this into the HubSpot notes.

Recommended eval matrix (two-track):
- Accuracy-first: Meta-OpenInstruction-v2 (or equivalent instruction-tuned LLM) — baseline for correctness, measured via labeled Q/A pairs and precision@k on retrieval-augmented prompts.
- Cost-first: Redwood-Quant-8b (8-bit quantized variant of an open decoder model) — baseline for per-token cost and throughput.

Benchmarks we will provide:
- Latency P50/P95 (token-level and request-level) across your typical query length distribution
- Cost per 1k tokens and cost per completed interaction (after reranking/recall)
- Quality metrics: exact match on labeled pairs, human eval score (1–5) on 200 sampled outputs, and a hallucination rate estimate using reference-based checks.
- Privacy checks: top-k token leakage metric (synthetic extraction tests) and redaction sensitivity flags when certain entity patterns are present.

Redaction guidance (brief):
- Remove direct identifiers (names, MRN, SSN) and free-text clinician notes containing provider identifiers.
- Replace structured IDs with stable pseudonyms (e.g., PATIENT_001) when needed for continuity.

Attachments: redwood_model_benchmark_2028-06.html (interactive report), lh_redaction_guidelines.pdf (draft).

Next steps we recommend: 
1) Emma shares 120 queries and 10 flagged edge cases by 6/26
2) Marissa & Grace will run an initial benchmark on the 120 set and return results + synthetic expansion plan by 7/2
3) Schedule a 30-minute review (7/6–7/8 window) to go through results and recommended production model.

Thanks — M.
Marissa Cole
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: redwood_model_benchmark_2028-06.html (html), lh_redaction_guidelines.pdf (pdf))

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Li <emma@lighthouse.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Lighthouse Health Procurement <procurement@lighthouse.health>
Date: Fri, 23 Jun 2028 10:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: next steps for eval prompts and sample set

Emma — thanks for confirming and for the sensitivity details. Quick operational notes and asks so both teams are aligned: 

- Please upload the 120 real queries to the Drive folder linked below or reply with the CSV attached. If any examples need second-party review, flag them in column E of the template.
- For redaction: we can run an automated scrub (PII/PHI detection) on your sample and produce a redaction report; to do this we need a signed DPA addendum — procurement, I'll loop you in separately to start that doc.
- Regarding model specifics: Marissa included the two recommended families. We will also test a middle-ground quantized instruction model if you’re open to a 3rd baseline — it often gives the best accuracy/cost tradeoff for healthcare Q/A workloads.

Please confirm: upload path (Drive) vs direct email attachment? Also, can procurement review the DPA by early next week (6/30) to avoid blocking the automated scrub?

Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AbCdef-ghIJkLMnop
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/76213

Action items (owner / due):
- Emma (Lighthouse): Upload 120 queries + mark sensitive rows / 2028-06-26
- Marissa (Redwood): Run initial benchmark on 6/26 sample / 2028-07-02
- Rafael (Redwood): Start DPA conversation with procurement / 2028-06-30

Thanks — looking forward to the samples.
Rafael
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: lh_sample_prompts_200.csv (csv), lh_redaction_guidelines.pdf (pdf))
